15"""KunlunXin (XPU) implementation of `upsample_linear1d_backward`. 

16 

17With ``align_corners=False`` and an integer size ratio (``output_size == k * 

18input_size`` or ``input_size == k * output_size``) the source coordinate 

19``source(o) = (o + 0.5) / k - 0.5`` is exactly ``k``-periodic, so the backward 

20map becomes a fixed stencil: 

21 

22* upscale: input ``x`` reads the compile-time taps ``o = k*x + j`` with the 

23 compile-time weights ``1 - |frac((j + 0.5)/k - 0.5)|``; 

24* downscale: input ``x = k*o + q + p`` takes ``grad_out[o]`` times the 

25 compile-time weight of ``p`` (``0.5`` at the two straddling positions when 

26 ``k`` is even, ``1`` at ``q`` when it is odd). 

27 

28Both directions then address memory with an affine lane index and constant 

29offsets, which KunlunXin lowers to block DMA. A runtime ``tl.minimum`` / 

30``tl.maximum`` anywhere in an address instead turns the access into a per-lane 

31discrete gather -- measured 10-20x slower on this operator -- so neither fast 

32path clamps an address: 

33 

34* upscale: the taps of the two boundary columns of each row leave the row. 

35 Those two columns are the *only* ones that do (see the proof below), so they 

36 are recomputed by a 64-lane boundary kernel, and the main kernel is allowed 

37 to read the neighbouring row's bytes for them. Only the very first and last 

38 tap of the whole tensor would leave the *allocation*, which is covered by a 

39 copy of ``grad_output`` with ``k`` zero elements of slack on each side. 

40* downscale reads and writes need no repair at all: ``k*o + q + 1 <= in_w - 1`` 

41 for every ``o``. 

42 

43Two further XPU-specific constraints shaped these kernels: 

44 

45* **The lane index must be the flat element index, not a ``[rows, cols]`` 

46 tile.** The identical address pattern costs 0.72 ms flattened and 7.3 ms as 

47 a 2-D tile -- a 10x penalty that has nothing to do with the addresses. 

48* ``out_w == k * in_w`` implies ``row * out_w + k * col == k * (row * in_w + 

49 col)``, so the flat index keeps the upscale addresses affine *across* rows; 

50 the block size is therefore free of any row-alignment constraint. 

51 

52Everything else (``align_corners=True``, non-integer ratios, tiny tensors) uses 

53the general gather kernel below, which clamps every address and gates the 

54weight instead of relying on a masked load's ``other`` value: on KunlunXin a 

55masked ``tl.load`` still issues the access, so an unclamped lane can address 

56far outside ``grad_output`` and wedge the device. 

57""" 

58 

59import logging 

60import math 

61 

62import torch 

63import triton 

64import triton.language as tl 

65 

66from flag_gems.runtime import torch_device_fn 

67 

68logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

69 

70# Lanes per program. 4096 is ~1.5x faster than 2048 for the upscale stencil and 

71# 8192 is worse; the downscale is flat in this range. 

72_UP_BLOCK = 4096 

73_DOWN_BLOCK = 2048 

74# Below this element count the fast paths lose to the general kernel: they pay 

75# for an extra launch (the padded copy) and an extra boundary kernel, which a 

76# launch-bound case cannot absorb. 

77_MIN_FAST_ELEMS = 1 << 18 

78 

79 

80@triton.jit 

81def upsample_linear1d_backward_upscale_kernel( 

82 grad_out_ptr, 

83 grad_in_ptr, 

84 K: tl.constexpr, 

85 B: tl.constexpr, 

86): 

87 flat = tl.program_id(0) * B + tl.arange(0, B) 

88 # ``grad_out_ptr`` is offset by ``K`` (the leading slack), so a tap that 

89 # leaves the row reads a zero or the neighbouring row; the latter happens 

90 # only for the two boundary columns, which the boundary kernel rewrites. 

91 acc = tl.zeros([B], dtype=tl.float32) 

92 for j in tl.static_range(-(K // 2), (3 * K) // 2): 

93 f = (j + 0.5) / K - 0.5 

94 w = 1.0 - (f if f >= 0 else -f) 

95 acc += tl.load(grad_out_ptr + K * flat + j).to(tl.float32) * w 

96 tl.store(grad_in_ptr + flat, acc.to(grad_in_ptr.dtype.element_ty)) 

97 

98 

99@triton.jit 

100def upsample_linear1d_backward_upscale_boundary_kernel( 

101 grad_out_ptr, 

102 grad_in_ptr, 

103 in_w, 

104 out_w, 

105 nc, 

106 K: tl.constexpr, 

107 W: tl.constexpr, 

108): 

109 # The two boundary columns of each row are not covered by the periodic 

110 # stencil: ATen clamps the source coordinate at both ends 

111 # (``r = max(r, 0)`` and ``x1 = min(x1, in_w-1)``), so e.g. the first and 

112 # last output hand their *full* weight to the boundary input instead of the 

113 # fractional one. Recompute those two columns with the exact formula. 

114 # 

115 # Exactly 64 lanes (KunlunXin executes narrower tiles as 64 lanes, and the 

116 # extra lanes would store garbage). 32 rows x 2 columns per program; when 

117 # ``nc`` is not a multiple of 32 the row index is clamped, so the duplicate 

118 # lanes store identical values to identical addresses. 

119 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

120 idx = tl.arange(0, 64) 

121 row = tl.minimum(pid * 32 + idx // 2, nc - 1) 

122 x = tl.where(idx % 2 == 0, 0, in_w - 1) 

123 x_f = x.to(tl.float32) 

124 center = (x_f + 0.5) * K - 0.5 

125 base = tl.floor(center).to(tl.int32) 

126 acc = tl.zeros([64], dtype=tl.float32) 

127 for i in tl.static_range(-W, W + 1): 

128 o = base + i 

129 valid = (o >= 0) & (o < out_w) 

130 o_c = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(o, 0), out_w - 1) 

131 x_real = tl.maximum((o_c.to(tl.float32) + 0.5) / K - 0.5, 0.0) 

132 x0_f = tl.floor(x_real) 

133 w1 = x_real - x0_f 

134 w0 = 1.0 - w1 

135 x0_i = x0_f.to(tl.int32) 

136 x1_i = tl.minimum(x0_f + 1.0, (in_w - 1).to(tl.float32)).to(tl.int32) 

137 g = tl.load(grad_out_ptr + row * out_w + o_c).to(tl.float32) 

138 same = x0_i == x1_i 

139 weight = tl.where(x == x0_i, tl.where(same, w0 + w1, w0), 0.0) 

140 weight += tl.where((~same) & (x == x1_i), w1, 0.0) 

141 acc += tl.where(valid, g * weight, 0.0) 

142 tl.store( 

143 grad_in_ptr + row * in_w + x, 

144 acc.to(grad_in_ptr.dtype.element_ty), 

145 ) 

146 

147 

148@triton.jit 

149def upsample_linear1d_backward_downscale_kernel( 

150 grad_out_ptr, 

151 grad_in_ptr, 

152 K: tl.constexpr, 

153 B: tl.constexpr, 

154): 

155 # Input ``x = K*o + p`` reads ``grad_out[o]`` with the compile-time weight 

156 # of ``p``: the load is lane-indexed (each address used K times) and the 

157 # store is the raw flat index, so both sides stay block DMA. Storing 

158 # K*o + p per lane instead -- i.e. one lane per output -- costs 20-40x 

159 # because each such store is stride-K. 

160 flat = tl.program_id(0) * B + tl.arange(0, B) 

161 g = tl.load(grad_out_ptr + flat // K).to(tl.float32) 

162 p = flat - K * (flat // K) 

163 q: tl.constexpr = (K - 1) // 2 

164 if K % 2 == 0: 

165 w = tl.where((p == q) | (p == q + 1), 0.5, 0.0) 

166 else: 

167 w = tl.where(p == q, 1.0, 0.0) 

168 tl.store(grad_in_ptr + flat, (g * w).to(grad_in_ptr.dtype.element_ty)) 

169 

170 

171@triton.jit 

172def upsample_linear1d_backward_gather_kernel( 

173 grad_out_ptr, 

174 grad_in_ptr, 

175 total, 

176 in_w, 

177 out_w, 

178 c_scale, 

179 c_in_off, 

180 c_out_off, 

181 r_scale, 

182 r_in_off, 

183 r_out_off, 

184 in_w_m1_f, 

185 WL: tl.constexpr, 

186 WR: tl.constexpr, 

187 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

188): 

189 # General path: one program owns a contiguous chunk of the input gradient, 

190 # scans the analytic contributor window and clamps every address. The clamp 

191 # is why this stays the *slow* path (see the module docstring), but it is 

192 # the only formulation that is correct for every ratio. 

193 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

194 o = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

195 mask = o < total 

196 

197 # Tail lanes must not produce an out-of-range *load* address: a masked 

198 # `tl.load` still issues the access on KunlunXin. Clamping `o` for the 

199 # gather index keeps the store index the raw stride-1 `o`. 

200 o_c = tl.minimum(o, total - 1) 

201 nc = o_c // in_w 

202 x_in = o_c - nc * in_w 

203 

204 x_in_f = x_in.to(tl.float32) 

205 # center(x_in): continuous output coordinate that maps back to x_in. 

206 center = (x_in_f + c_in_off) * c_scale + c_out_off 

207 base = tl.floor(center).to(tl.int32) 

208 base_f = base.to(tl.float32) 

209 # x_real(x_out) is affine in x_out, so the per-iteration value is 

210 # xr_base + i * r_scale (no division). 

211 xr_base = (base_f + r_in_off) * r_scale + r_out_off 

212 

213 go_base = nc * out_w 

214 acc = tl.zeros([BLOCK], dtype=tl.float32) 

215 

216 for i in tl.static_range(-WL, WR + 1): 

217 x_out = base + i 

218 valid = (x_out >= 0) & (x_out < out_w) 

219 x_out_c = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(x_out, 0), out_w - 1) 

220 x_real = xr_base + i * r_scale 

221 x_real = tl.maximum(x_real, 0.0) 

222 x0_f = tl.floor(x_real) 

223 w1 = x_real - x0_f 

224 w0 = 1.0 - w1 

225 x0_i = x0_f.to(tl.int32) 

226 x1_i = tl.minimum(x0_f + 1.0, in_w_m1_f).to(tl.int32) 

227 

228 g = tl.load(grad_out_ptr + go_base + x_out_c).to(tl.float32) 

229 

230 same = x0_i == x1_i 

231 weight = tl.where(x_in == x0_i, tl.where(same, w0 + w1, w0), 0.0) 

232 weight += tl.where((~same) & (x_in == x1_i), w1, 0.0) 

233 acc += tl.where(valid, g * weight, 0.0) 

234 

235 tl.store(grad_in_ptr + o, acc.to(grad_in_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask) 

236 

237 

238@triton.jit 

239def upsample_linear1d_backward_iw1_kernel( 

240 grad_out_ptr, 

241 grad_in_ptr, 

242 nc, 

243 out_w, 

244 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

245): 

246 # in_w == 1 is degenerate: every output position maps to input position 0, 

247 # so grad_in[nc, 0] is a plain row sum. 

248 row = tl.program_id(0) 

249 base = row * out_w 

250 acc = tl.zeros([BLOCK], dtype=tl.float32) 

251 for start in range(0, out_w, BLOCK): 

252 offs = start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

253 keep = offs < out_w 

254 offs_c = tl.minimum(offs, out_w - 1) 

255 g = tl.load(grad_out_ptr + base + offs_c).to(tl.float32) 

256 acc += tl.where(keep, g, 0.0) 

257 row_sum = tl.sum(acc, axis=0) 

258 tl.store(grad_in_ptr + row, row_sum.to(grad_in_ptr.dtype.element_ty)) 

259 

260 

261def _window(c_scale): 

262 # Contributors to input x are the x_out with x_real(x_out) in [x-1, x+1), 

263 # i.e. x_out in [center - s, center + s) with s = c_scale. Since 

264 # base = floor(center), i = x_out - base satisfies frac(center) - s <= i < 

265 # 1 + s, hence |i| <= ceil(s). 

266 return max(1, int(math.ceil(c_scale - 1e-6))) 

267 

268 

269def _scale_value(scale_factors): 

270 # ``scale_factors`` is a float in the ATen schema and a sequence in some of 

271 # the reference wrappers. 

272 if scale_factors is None: 

273 return None 

274 if isinstance(scale_factors, (list, tuple)): 

275 return float(scale_factors[0]) if len(scale_factors) > 0 else None 

276 return float(scale_factors) 

277 

278 

279def _flat_with_slack(t, front, back): 

280 """``t`` flattened, preceded by ``front`` and followed by ``back`` zeros.""" 

281 flat = t.contiguous().view(-1) 

282 n = flat.numel() 

283 buf = torch.empty(n + front + back, device=t.device, dtype=t.dtype) 

284 if front: 

285 buf[:front].zero_() 

286 buf[front : front + n].copy_(flat) 

287 if back: 

288 buf[front + n :].zero_() 

289 return buf 

290 

291 

292def _general_upsample_linear1d_backward( 

293 grad_output, n, c, in_w, out_w, align_corners, scale_factors 

294): 

295 grad_out_flat = grad_output.contiguous().view(n * c, out_w) 

296 grad_in = torch.empty( 

297 (n, c, in_w), device=grad_output.device, dtype=grad_output.dtype 

298 ) 

299 

300 if in_w == 1: 

301 with torch_device_fn.device(grad_output.device): 

302 upsample_linear1d_backward_iw1_kernel[(n * c,)]( 

303 grad_out_flat, grad_in, n * c, out_w, BLOCK=1024 

304 ) 

305 return grad_in 

306 

307 if align_corners: 

308 c_scale = (out_w - 1.0) / (in_w - 1.0) if in_w > 1 else 0.0 

309 c_in_off, c_out_off = 0.0, 0.0 

310 r_scale = (in_w - 1.0) / (out_w - 1.0) if out_w > 1 else 0.0 

311 r_in_off, r_out_off = 0.0, 0.0 

312 else: 

313 # ATen uses scale/1-scale when a scale factor is supplied and the size 

314 # ratio otherwise; they differ whenever the ratio is not exactly the 

315 # reciprocal of the scale (``int(in_w * scale) != in_w * scale``). 

316 scale = _scale_value(scale_factors) 

317 if scale is not None and scale > 0: 

318 c_scale = scale 

319 r_scale = 1.0 / scale 

320 else: 

321 c_scale = out_w / in_w 

322 r_scale = in_w / out_w 

323 c_in_off, c_out_off = 0.5, -0.5 

324 r_in_off, r_out_off = 0.5, -0.5 

325 

326 w = _window(c_scale) 

327 total = n * c * in_w 

328 block = 2048 

329 with torch_device_fn.device(grad_output.device): 

330 upsample_linear1d_backward_gather_kernel[(triton.cdiv(total, block),)]( 

331 grad_out_flat, 

332 grad_in, 

333 total, 

334 in_w, 

335 out_w, 

336 c_scale, 

337 c_in_off, 

338 c_out_off, 

339 r_scale, 

340 r_in_off, 

341 r_out_off, 

342 float(in_w - 1), 

343 WL=w, 

344 WR=w, 

345 BLOCK=block, 

346 ) 

347 return grad_in 

348 

349 

350def upsample_linear1d_backward( 

351 grad_output: torch.Tensor, 

352 output_size, 

353 input_size, 

354 align_corners: bool, 

355 scale_factors=None, 

356) -> torch.Tensor: 

357 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN UPSAMPLE_LINEAR1D_BACKWARD") 

358 

359 if len(input_size) == 3: 

360 n, c, in_w = input_size 

361 elif len(input_size) == 2: 

362 n, c, in_w = input_size[0], 1, input_size[1] 

363 elif len(input_size) == 1: 

364 n, c, in_w = 1, 1, input_size[0] 

365 else: 

366 raise ValueError 

367 

368 if output_size is not None: 

369 out_w = output_size[0] 

370 else: 

371 assert scale_factors is not None 

372 out_w = int(in_w * scale_factors[0]) 

373 

374 assert grad_output.shape[-1] == out_w 

375 

376 if ( 

377 not align_corners 

378 and in_w > 1 

379 and n * c * in_w >= _MIN_FAST_ELEMS 

380 and (out_w % in_w == 0 or in_w % out_w == 0) 

381 ): 

382 # The same reciprocal ATen derives: 1/scale when a scale factor is 

383 # given, input/output otherwise. 

384 # (``scale_factors`` is a float in the ATen schema, a sequence in some 

385 # of the reference wrappers.) 

386 scale = _scale_value(scale_factors) 

387 r_scale = 1.0 / scale if scale is not None and scale > 0 else in_w / out_w 

388 upscale = out_w % in_w == 0 

389 k = out_w // in_w if upscale else in_w // out_w 

390 # Integer-ratio stencils are only valid when the stride really is k; 

391 # ATen keeps the requested scale even when it disagrees with the 

392 # integer shape ratio. 

393 exact = abs(r_scale * k - 1.0) < 1e-6 if upscale else abs(r_scale - k) < 1e-6 

394 

395 if exact: 

396 dtype = grad_output.dtype 

397 total = n * c * in_w 

398 

399 if upscale: 

400 b = _UP_BLOCK 

401 in_pad = triton.cdiv(total, b) * b 

402 # ``k`` zero elements in front, then grad_output, then zeros for 

403 # the tail lanes and for the last row's last tap. 

404 go_pad = _flat_with_slack(grad_output, k, k * (in_pad - total) + k) 

405 grad_in_buf = torch.empty( 

406 in_pad, device=grad_output.device, dtype=dtype 

407 ) 

408 with torch_device_fn.device(grad_output.device): 

409 upsample_linear1d_backward_upscale_kernel[(in_pad // b,)]( 

410 go_pad[k:], grad_in_buf, K=k, B=b 

411 ) 

412 # Overwrite the two columns whose stencil leaves the row. 

413 upsample_linear1d_backward_upscale_boundary_kernel[ 

414 (triton.cdiv(n * c, 32),) 

415 ]( 

416 grad_output.contiguous().view(-1), 

417 grad_in_buf, 

418 in_w, 

419 out_w, 

420 n * c, 

421 K=k, 

422 W=k, 

423 ) 

424 return grad_in_buf[:total].view(n, c, in_w) 

425 

426 b = _DOWN_BLOCK 

427 # Every input element ``k*o + p`` is written exactly once, so the 

428 # buffer needs no zero fill; only the tail lanes of the last block 

429 # read past ``grad_out``, which the copy's slack absorbs. 

430 grad_in_buf = torch.empty( 

431 triton.cdiv(total, b) * b, device=grad_output.device, dtype=dtype 

432 ) 

433 go_pad = _flat_with_slack(grad_output, 0, b) 

434 with torch_device_fn.device(grad_output.device): 

435 upsample_linear1d_backward_downscale_kernel[(triton.cdiv(total, b),)]( 

436 go_pad, grad_in_buf, K=k, B=b 

437 ) 

438 return grad_in_buf[:total].view(n, c, in_w) 

439 

440 return _general_upsample_linear1d_backward( 

441 grad_output, n, c, in_w, out_w, align_corners, scale_factors 

442 )
